title: 数字生活与社会词汇
goal: 理解数字生活词汇及技术使用的便利和条件。

points.label: 识别数字生活词汇及搭配
读懂技术影响与限制条件

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲（2016年修订版）

body.p: 数字技术影响信息获取、线上交流和个人数据的使用。阅读这类文章时，要分清技术带来的便利、它的限制和适用条件。

body.box: An online notice can reach residents quickly, but it helps only those who can access it.

body.p: reach residents quickly 是便利。only those who can access it 限定了受益的人。

cards.title: 词汇表：信息获取
rows: The library provides access to online journals.
Readers search the catalogue by title.
The website lists the opening hours.
The page opens in a browser.
Staff upload the schedule each week.
The link leads to the catalogue.
The guide can be read on a mobile device.
The school network connects the computers.
The online catalogue includes old maps.
The offline copy can be read without a connection.

cards.title: 词汇表：线上交流
rows: The platform hosts the group's discussions.
She sent a message to the group.
A reader added a comment below the post.
The organizer replied to the question.
Participants share notes after the meeting.
Members can contact the organizer by email.
Each participant received a meeting link.
The schedule appeared on the screen.
The message contained text and a picture.
Email is one channel for announcements.
The organizer will notify members of changes.

cards.title: 词汇表：个人数据
rows: The policy explains how the service protects privacy.
The form asks for personal details.
The form collects data about attendance.
The app requests permission to use the camera.
The organizers asked for consent before sharing names.
A password can help protect an account.
The service stores the files online.
A member can delete an old message.
A setting controls who can see the post.
The group keeps its member list private.
The public notice contains no phone numbers.

body.box: A neighborhood group uses an online platform to arrange shared meals. Members post times and reply when they can attend. This allows people to coordinate without meeting in person first. However, a member who has no internet connection may miss a change posted shortly before the meal. The organizer therefore also provides a telephone contact. Members choose whether to share their phone numbers with the group; the public notice contains only the meal time and place.

body.p: post times 和 reply 说明平台如何帮助安排聚餐。without meeting in person first 指出便利。
no internet connection may miss a change 说明限制。telephone contact 为无法及时查看平台的成员提供另一种联系渠道。
choose whether to share their phone numbers 说明是否公开号码由成员自己决定。public notice 只写时间和地点。

groups.fill: A local library provides an online catalogue. Readers can sea{rch} by title and follow a li{nk} to a book's record. A digital dev{ice}, such as a phone, can open the page. Members with an acc{ount} can save a list of titles. The library asks for permi{ssion} before sending messages, and a privacy set{ting} controls who can see the list. Readers may del{ete} old titles, down{load} the list, sh{are} it with friends, or use an off{line} copy without a connection.
notes: search：by title 表示按标题搜索。
device：手机是可打开页面的设备。
setting：隐私设置控制可见范围。
share：with friends 表示与朋友分享。
offline：without a connection 表示离线使用。

groups.text:
A neighborhood repair group uses an online message board to arrange visits. Residents post descriptions of broken objects, and volunteers reply with times when they are available. The board makes it possible to compare suggestions before choosing a time. It also keeps earlier replies in one place, so a resident can return to them later.

The system has limits. A resident who cannot use the board may not see a volunteer's reply. The group therefore leaves a telephone number at a local shop, where residents can ask for help arranging a visit. Volunteers check the telephone messages as well as the board before confirming their plans.

The group asks residents to describe an object without publishing their home address. After a volunteer and resident agree on a visit, they exchange the address privately. The public board shows the kind of object and the proposed time, but not the address. This arrangement lets members discuss repairs while limiting the personal information shown to everyone.

items.stem: What does a volunteer's reply provide?
options: A time when the volunteer is available
A public list of all residents' addresses
A record of the shop's opening hours
A description of the broken object
items.why: volunteers reply with times when they are available 说明回复提供可用时间。

items.stem: What does the board allow residents to do?
options: Avoid describing the objects that need repair
Compare suggestions before selecting a time
Receive a visit without confirming a plan
Read private addresses on the public board
items.why: compare suggestions before choosing a time 说明可先比较建议。

items.stem: What does 'privately' mean in the final paragraph?
options: On a board visible to everyone
Without agreeing on a visit
Between the people concerned
Inside the local shop's notice
items.why: public board ... not the address 表明地址仅在有关人员之间交换。

items.stem: Why does the group provide a telephone number?
options: To replace volunteers' repair suggestions
To keep residents' home addresses off the public board
To let volunteers confirm visits without the board
To offer contact to people unable to use the board
items.why: A resident who cannot use the board may not see a volunteer's reply 之后的 therefore 引出电话。第三项不对：志愿者确认前电话和留言板都要查看。

items.stem: What information appears on the public board?
options: The resident's full home address
The object type and proposed time
The private telephone messages
The telephone number left at the shop
items.why: public board shows the kind of object and the proposed time 说明公开信息的范围。

groups.fill: A school group shares a digital calendar. Each member has an acc{ount} and signs in with a pass{word}. The calendar's privacy set{ting} determines who may see an event. Members can upl{oad} a schedule, upd{ate} its time, and del{ete} an event that is cancelled. They can also send a mes{sage} to partic{ipants}. A member who is off{line} cannot see a change until the dev{ice} connects again, so the organizer also posts a paper schedule.

groups.text:
A town museum introduced an online platform for people interested in local history. Members can share photographs and add descriptions of places they recognize. Museum staff check the descriptions against their records before adding them to a public collection. This process brings together information from people who might not otherwise meet. It also lets members contribute at a time that suits them.

The platform does not reach every resident. Some people do not have a reliable connection at home, and others prefer to bring photographs to the museum. Staff therefore continue to accept contributions in person. They make a digital copy with the owner's agreement and return the original. Both online and in-person contributions are reviewed before publication.

The museum also gives contributors a choice about personal information. A contributor can allow a name to appear beside a photograph or ask for the photograph to be published without a name. Staff do not publish a home address as part of the collection. The platform offers a convenient way to contribute, but the museum's other arrangements remain necessary for people who cannot or do not wish to use it.

items.stem: What does the platform enable members to do?
options: Share photographs and describe locations
Publish every description without review
Borrow original photographs from residents
Replace the museum's public collection
items.why: 依据是 share photographs and add descriptions of places they recognize，第一项用 describe locations 改写了后半句。

items.stem: What does 'contribute' mean in this passage?
options: Remove a reviewed photograph
Provide material for the collection
Restrict access to the platform
Return a visitor's original photograph
items.why: contributions 指居民提供的照片等资料，对应为馆藏提供材料。

items.stem: Why does the museum accept photographs in person?
options: Every member wants a name beside a photograph
Staff cannot review online contributions
Some residents lack a connection or prefer visiting
Residents must leave their originals with the museum
items.why: Some people do not have a reliable connection 和 others prefer to bring photographs to the museum 是线下收照片的两个原因，第三项把两者都包括了。

items.stem: Which detail can a contributor choose to omit from publication?
options: The historical place shown in every picture
The museum's records about a photograph
The museum's review of the submitted description
The contributor's name beside the photograph
items.why: allow a name to appear 或 published without a name 说明投稿者可选择是否署名。

items.stem: What does 'public' mean for the collection?
options: Kept only in a contributor's home
Available for people generally to see
Exchanged only between two staff members
Stored without any descriptions of places
items.why: public collection 指向公众开放的馆藏；公开姓名由投稿者选择。
